absent: Allocation, free, reclaim, compaction and slab object behaviour beyond the node descriptor fields shown.
Layout and locking of struct zone, zonelist construction, and first and next pgdat and zone traversal.
Sparse section initialization, hotplug resize implementation, and vmemmap population.
Kswapd and kcompactd wakeup, scheduling, progress and failure accounting dynamics.
NUMA balancing promotion limits, memory tier selection, and per-CPU node statistic accounting.

findings.text: The pglist_data structure, also called pg_data_t, centralizes node state around node_zones and node_zonelists with nr_zones counting populated entries, flatmem pointers such as node_mem_map, range counters node_start_pfn with node_present_pages and node_spanned_pages plus node_id, wait queues for kswapd and reclaim throttling with related counters, daemon state for kswapd and optional kcompactd, totalreserve_pages and NUMA minima, deferred-init and balancing cursors, an embedded lruvec with flags, and statistics in per_cpu_nodestats with vm_stat plus optional tier and failure records.

When hotplug or deferred structure init is enabled, node_size_lock serializes observers of node_start_pfn, node_present_pages, node_spanned_pages, nr_zones and first_deferred_pfn so those values stay stable across the critical section, with dedicated resize helpers provided to acquire it without testing configuration, and ordering requires holding it above zone lock and span seqlock.

Per-node accessors resolve through NODE_DATA for the given id, with present reporting usable page count and spanned reporting address span including holes; end position derives as start plus spanned via pgdat_end_pfn and the node_end_pfn accessor.
Hopeless-clear reasons form an ordered four-value enumeration beginning at zero for OTHER then KSWAPD, DIRECT and PCP; memory init context distinguishes EARLY boot from HOTPLUG paths.

local_memory_node returns its input unchanged; zone_idx derives an index by offsetting a zone pointer from its node base array; zone_is_zone_device reports whether that index equals the device zone in one configuration and always reports false in the other; managed_zone reports true when managed page count is nonzero; populated_zone reports true when present page count is nonzero.

Node association either reads and writes a per-zone node field or collapses to constant zero with a no-op setter when NUMA is absent; highmem classification checks for the highmem index and optionally the movable zone alias, lifted from index to zone pointer; DMA availability reports whether the DMA zone is managed when that zone exists and false otherwise.

Online node iteration walks a pgdat chain from first to next; zone iteration walks a global zone chain starting at the first online node base, with a populated variant skipping zones whose present count is empty; zoneref accessors expose the referenced zone, its cached zone index and its node derived through the zone to node mapping.

Filtered zonelist walks start at the list head and advance past entries above a highest index or outside an optional nodemask, with a fast path when no mask is given and the current index already qualifies; iteration macros bind both cursor and zone on each step, including a null-mask shorthand and a resume-from-cursor form; movable-only detection returns false for an empty mask and otherwise probes the fallback list of an arbitrary masked node for any zone at or below NORMAL, reporting true only when none qualifies.

Section geometry derives physical and frame-number shifts from section size and page shift, with total section count, pages per section and an inverted alignment mask expressed as powers of two; block-flag storage scales with pageblock order and per-block bits; subsection geometry uses a fixed shift with corresponding size, frame shift, count and mask; subsections per section relate the two sizes; root packing either divides page size by section descriptor size or fixes one per root, with helpers for root index, root count rounding up and in-root mask.

Usage records pair an RCU callback head with an optional subsection existence bitmap sized to subsections per section and a trailing variable-length pageblock flag array also reachable as a usemap pointer; section descriptors hold an encoded map word mixing pointer with flag and early node bits, a usage pointer and optional page extension state with padding, constrained to power-of-two size so root masking works; subsection alignment helpers round frame numbers up or down to subsection multiples.

Frame number and section number convert by shifting with the section frame shift, with helpers aligning a frame number up or down to section boundaries; section index maps to a descriptor through root division plus in-root offset, rejecting out-of-range roots and missing extreme roots with null; map address extraction masks away low flag bits; frame to section composes number conversion with index lookup; subsection position derives from the in-section offset divided by subsection size.

Low map-word bits encode marked present, has map, online and early states, with optional device taint and preinitialized vmemmap bits where configured, terminated by a last-bit marker; each state has a single-bit mask, a combined map mask preserves only high pointer bits, and the node-id shift equals the last-bit position to allow early node encoding.

Presence, validity, earliness and online state each test the corresponding map bit with null tolerance, with numbered variants resolving the descriptor first; device online additionally requires the taint bit in one configuration and always fails in the other; preinit state either tests its bit or always fails with a no-op early init; subsection checks either consult the bitmap with single and first-valid-plus-advance forms or always succeed; frame validity rejects upper-bit mismatch and out-of-range sections then under scheduler RCU requires a mapped section that is early or subsection-valid; helpers find the first valid frame in a range, step to the next valid frame with a same-subsection fast path, iterate present sections and valid frames, and map frames to nodes as constant zero or through the page.

This configuration fixes both total and online node counts to one, guarded by a conventional include sentinel; print support expands a mask into a count plus bit pointer, yielding zero and null for a null input and the configured count with bit storage otherwise.

Callers must handle null from out-of-range or unpopulated section roots and null usage as absence rather than validity; early sections treat a whole section span as valid even when subsections lack bitmap entries; validity and first-valid scans require holding scheduler read protection across the valid-plus-subsection test; next-frame optimization must use the subsection mask only when vmemmap subsection tracking is enabled and the section mask otherwise.
